1670	### Processing tasks
1671	
1672	A processing task is a named unit of work attached to a schema version; each
1673	run records one attempt. Tasks and runs are persisted across restarts.
1674	
1675	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks` — create a
1676	  task. Body: `{"name": "extract", "depends_on": [1], "max_attempts": 3}`.
1677	  `name` must be non-empty and unique within the version (`409` on conflict);
1678	  `depends_on` is an array of distinct task ids from the same version (default
1679	  `[]`, unknown ids → `404`); `max_attempts` is a positive integer (default
1680	  `1`). Returns `201` with `id`, `dataset`, `version`, `name`, `depends_on`,
1681	  `max_attempts`, `status` (`pending`), `attempt_count` (`0`) and
1682	  `created_at`. Other invalid input → `422` and nothing is written.
1683	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks` — list tasks
1684	  sorted by `id` ascending.
1685	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}` —
1686	  return the task together with its `runs`, sorted by `attempt` ascending.
1687	  Each run has `id`, `task_id`, `attempt`, `status`, `started_at`,
1688	  `finished_at` and `error`. Unknown dataset/version/task → `404`.
1689	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}/runs` —
1690	  start a new run. Only allowed while the task is `pending` or `failed`, has
1691	  attempts left (`attempt_count < max_attempts`) and every task in
1692	  `depends_on` has status `succeeded`; otherwise `409` and nothing is written.
1693	  Returns `201` with the new `running` run and increments the task's
1694	  `attempt_count` (the task becomes `running`).
1695	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/dispatch` —
1696	  worker batch claim. The body is optional and contains only an optional
1697	  `limit`: omit the body (or send `{}`) to claim one task, or send
1698	  `{"limit": <positive integer>}`. Within a single transaction, up to `limit`
1699	  startable tasks are selected by task id ascending; a task is startable when
1700	  it is `pending`, or `failed` with attempts left, and every direct dependency
1701	  is `succeeded` at selection time. Each selected task gets a new `running`
1702	  run for its next attempt, `attempt_count` is incremented and the task becomes
1703	  `running`. `running`, `succeeded`, attempt-exhausted and dependency-blocked
1704	  tasks are skipped; a task started earlier in the same request is only
1705	  `running`, so its dependents are not selectable until a later request.
1706	  Returns `201` with `{"dataset", "version", "runs"}`; `runs` is sorted by
1707	  task id ascending and each run has the same fields as the single-task start
1708	  endpoint. When no task is startable the response is still `201` with an
1709	  empty `runs` list. Concurrent dispatches (and dispatches interleaved with
1710	  single-task starts) never create a duplicate attempt or two running runs for
1711	  the same task, and a single response never exceeds `limit`. Unknown
1712	  dataset/version → `404`; extra body fields, a non-integer (including
1713	  boolean) or non-positive `limit` → `422` and nothing is written.
1714	- `PATCH /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}/runs/{run_id}` —
1715	  finish the currently running run. Body: `{"status": "succeeded"}` or
1716	  `{"status": "failed", "error": "<non-empty message>"}`. Writes `finished_at`
1717	  and moves the task to the same status; a `failed` task with attempts left
1718	  can be started again. Finishing an already finished run → `409`; a run that
1719	  does not belong to the task/version in the path → `422`; unknown
1720	  dataset/version/task/run → `404`; other invalid input → `422` and nothing
1721	  is written.
1722	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/batch-complete` —
1723	  finish several currently running runs in one transaction. Body contains only
1724	  a non-empty `runs` array; each item names a task of the path version and one
1725	  of its runs: `{"task_id": <int>, "run_id": <int>, "status": "succeeded"}` or
1726	  the same with `"status": "failed"` and an `error` that is non-empty after
1727	  trimming whitespace (`succeeded` items carry no `error`). The same task must
1728	  not appear twice. The whole batch is validated before any write and either
1729	  every item completes or none do; on success the response is
1730	  `{"dataset", "version", "runs"}` with the completed runs sorted by task id
1731	  ascending, each carrying the same fields as the single-run finish response.
1732	  Every run gets a `finished_at` timestamp and its task moves atomically to
1733	  the same status; `failed` tasks keep their consumed attempts and stay
1734	  retryable while attempts remain. Tasks whose dependencies succeed in the
1735	  same batch are not started or skipped within that batch (the dependencies
1736	  are `running` at selection time, as with dispatch) and become startable
1737	  immediately afterwards, each at its next continuous attempt. Empty/missing
1738	  `runs`, extra fields, non-integer (including boolean) ids, an unknown status
1739	  or a missing/blank/non-string `error` → `422`; an empty body or malformed
1740	  JSON → `422`; any query parameter → `422`. Unknown dataset/version → `404`;
1741	  a batch task that does not exist or belongs to another dataset/version →
1742	  `404`; an unknown run → `404` (a run belonging to another dataset/version is
1743	  treated as out of scope); a run that belongs to another task of the same
1744	  version → `422`. An already finished run, a duplicate task in the batch or a
1745	  task that is not currently `running` (not currently completable) → `409`,
1746	  and the entire batch is rolled back: statuses, timestamps and counters are
1747	  unchanged. Concurrent batch completion is single-winner against the
1748	  single-run finish/cancel endpoints, run starts and batch dispatch: exactly
1749	  one racing operation commits and the others receive `409`, never leaving a
1750	  `running` run with a half-written `finished_at` or rolling `attempt_count`
1751	  back. Audit records appended afterwards record the run's terminal status,
1752	  and the schedule, audit report and post-restart reads present the batch
1753	  results through the existing fields and ordering.
1754	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}/runs/{run_id}/cancel` —
1755	  cancel the currently running run. The body contains only a non-empty
1756	  `reason` string; leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed and the result
1757	  is stored as the run's `error`. Returns the updated run with `finished_at`
1758	  written and `status` `failed`; the task is atomically moved to `failed` in
1759	  the same transaction while `attempt_count` is not rolled back, so a
1760	  cancelled task follows the existing start rules: it can run again when its
1761	  dependencies have succeeded and attempts remain, and the next run keeps the
1762	  continuous attempt sequence. Only a `running` run can be cancelled;
1763	  cancelling an already `succeeded`/`failed` run returns `409` and changes no
1764	  field. A run that does not belong to the task/version in the path → `422`;
1765	  unknown dataset/version/task/run → `404`; a missing reason, an extra body
1766	  field, a non-string reason or one that is blank after trimming, an empty
1767	  body, malformed JSON or any query parameter → `422` and nothing is
1768	  written. Cancellation is single-winner against finishing, single-task
1769	  starts and batch dispatch: exactly one racing operation performs the state
1770	  transition and the others receive `409`, so no run is left `running` with a
1771	  half-written `finished_at`.
1772	- `PUT /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}/dependencies` —
1773	  atomically replace the task's dependency list. Body contains only
1774	  `{"depends_on": [<task id>, ...]}` (the array may be empty); the ids must
1775	  reference existing tasks of the same version without duplicates and must not
1776	  include the target task itself. The replacement is rejected when the target
1777	  task is not `pending` or when it would introduce a cycle in the dependency
1778	  graph; on success the updated task is returned. Unknown
1779	  dataset/version/task/dependency → `404`; a self dependency, a cycle or a
1780	  non-`pending` target → `409`; any other invalid body → `422` and nothing is
1781	  written. The existing run-start rule uses the updated dependencies.
1782	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/schedule` —
1783	  return `{"dataset", "version", "tasks"}` with tasks sorted by `id` ascending.
1784	  Each task carries every processing-task field plus `schedule_state` and
1785	  `blocking_task_ids`. `schedule_state` is `running` or `succeeded` for tasks
1786	  in those states; a `failed` task is `retryable` while attempts remain and
1787	  `exhausted` once they are used up; a `pending` task is `ready` when all of
1788	  its direct dependencies have succeeded, `upstream_failed` when any
1789	  dependency chain contains an `exhausted` or `upstream_failed` task, and
1790	  `blocked` otherwise. `blocking_task_ids` lists the direct dependencies that
1791	  have not succeeded, sorted ascending; it is empty for non-pending tasks.
1792	  States are recomputed on every read (including after a successful retry)
1793	  and both the dependency graph and the schedule survive restarts.
1794	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/audit-report` —
1795	  read-only audit report for the whole version; the endpoint takes no request
1796	  body and no query parameters (both are rejected with `422`; unknown
1797	  dataset/version → `404`). Returns
1798	  `{"dataset", "version", "summary", "tasks"}`. `summary` contains
1799	  `task_count`, `run_count`, `pending_tasks`, `running_tasks`,
1800	  `succeeded_tasks`, `failed_tasks`, `exhausted_tasks` and
1801	  `invalid_audit_runs`; status counters count tasks by their stored status,
1802	  `exhausted_tasks` counts `failed` tasks that have used up
1803	  `max_attempts`, and `invalid_audit_runs` counts runs whose audit chain fails
1804	  re-verification. `tasks` is sorted by task `id` and each task carries every
1805	  processing-task field plus `runs`; `runs` is sorted by `attempt` and each
1806	  run carries its run fields plus `proof`. `proof` re-runs the same checks as
1807	  the per-run verify endpoint over that run's audit chain and is
1808	  `{"valid", "checked_count", "last_evidence_hash"}`; `last_evidence_hash` is
1809	  the stored evidence hash of the chain's final record and is `null` only for
1810	  an empty chain — it is still returned when `valid` is `false`, and the run
1811	  details are retained. Summary counters always agree with the returned
1812	  details and the report is deterministic across restarts.
1813	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/processing-audit-export` — read-only cross-version
1814	  export of the dataset's whole processing audit state, computed fresh on
1815	  every read (no caching; nothing is written, modified or deleted, and no
1816	  task, run or audit record is touched). The path carries only the dataset
1817	  name; the request takes no body and no query parameters — any body bytes,
1818	  including a purely whitespace or single-space body, or any query parameter
1819	  → `422`; an unknown dataset → `404`, with the same 404-before-422
1820	  precedence as the compliance exports. A dataset without schema versions
1821	  returns `200` with an empty `versions` array and all-zero totals, never an
1822	  error. The JSON document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact
1823	  whitespace, exactly one trailing newline):
1824	
1825	  ```json
1826	  {"dataset":"orders","versions":[{"version":1,"task_count":3,"run_count":3,"invalid_audit_runs":0,"terminal_tasks":{"succeeded_tasks":1,"failed_tasks":1,"exhausted_tasks":1}}],"totals":{"version_count":1,"task_count":3,"run_count":3,"invalid_audit_runs":0,"succeeded_tasks":1,"failed_tasks":1,"exhausted_tasks":1}}
1827	  ```
1828	
1829	  The top-level keys are exactly `dataset`, `versions`, `totals` in that
1830	  order. `versions` is ordered by version number ascending and each entry has
1831	  exactly `version`, `task_count`, `run_count`, `invalid_audit_runs` and
1832	  `terminal_tasks` in that order; only counts and conclusions are exported,
1833	  never the per-task or per-run details of the per-version audit report.

1835	  under exactly the same criteria the per-version report and the per-run
1836	  verify read use (recomputed evidence hashes, continuous sequences from `1`

1840	  and `exhausted_tasks` — the succeeded and failed task counts plus the

1843	  terminal distribution. `totals` has exactly `version_count`,
1844	  `task_count`, `run_count`, `invalid_audit_runs`, `succeeded_tasks`,
1845	  `failed_tasks` and `exhausted_tasks`, each the sum of the matching
1846	  per-version values over the whole dataset.
1847	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/processing-blocker-summary` — read-only
1848	  cross-version summary of what keeps each version's processing tasks from
1849	  proceeding, computed fresh on every read (no caching; nothing is written,
1850	  modified or deleted, and no task, run, dependency or audit record is
1851	  touched). The path carries only the dataset name; the request takes no
1852	  body and no query parameters — any body bytes, including a purely
1853	  whitespace or single-space body, or any query parameter → `422`; an
1854	  unknown dataset → `404`, checked before the body/query validation. A
1855	  dataset without schema versions returns `200` with an empty `versions`
1856	  array and all-zero totals, never an error. The JSON document is
1857	  deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing
1858	  newline). The top-level keys are exactly `dataset`, `versions` and
1859	  `totals` in that order; `versions` is ordered by version number ascending
1860	  and each entry has exactly `version`, `tasks`, `ready_count`,
1861	  `running_count`, `succeeded_count`, `failed_count`, `exhausted_count` and
1862	  `blocked_count` in that order. `tasks` is ordered by task `id` ascending;
1863	  each task has exactly `id`, `name`, `status` (the stored task status),
1864	  `schedule_state`, `blocking_task_ids`, `cause` and `causes` in that
1865	  order. `schedule_state` uses the same seven literals and the same
1866	  derivation as the per-version schedule view (`running`, `succeeded`,
1867	  `retryable`, `exhausted`, `ready`, `blocked`, `upstream_failed`);
1868	  `blocking_task_ids` likewise lists the not-yet-succeeded direct
1869	  dependencies of a pending task, id-ascending and de-duplicated, and is an
1870	  empty array for every non-pending task. The blocker categories are
1871	  `direct_dependency` (a pending task still waiting on an unsucceeded
1872	  direct dependency), `upstream_failed` (a dependency chain is exhausted or
1873	  upstream-failed, at any distance) and `attempts_exhausted` (a `failed`
1874	  task that has used up `max_attempts`); the categories are independent, so
1875	  a pending task whose dependency chain failed hits both
1876	  `direct_dependency` and `upstream_failed`. `causes` lists every category
1877	  that applies in alphabetical order (an empty array when none applies),
1878	  and `cause` is the single highest-priority category —
1879	  `attempts_exhausted`, then `upstream_failed`, then `direct_dependency` —
1880	  or `null` when no category applies. The six counts partition the seven
1881	  schedule states into mutually exclusive buckets (the counts always sum to
1882	  the version's task count): `ready`, `running`, `succeeded` and `exhausted`
1883	  keep their own buckets, a `retryable` task is counted as `failed`, and
1884	  `blocked` together with `upstream_failed` is counted as `blocked`.
1885	  `totals` has exactly `version_count`, `task_count` and the six
1886	  `*_count` counters, each the sum of the matching per-version values.

1888	### Processing run audit records (append-only proof chain)
1889	
1890	Every run carries an independent, tamper-evident chain of audit records.
1891	Records are append-only (the database rejects updates and deletes, and there
1892	are no per-record HTTP routes), numbered from `1` per run and linked through
1893	SHA-256 evidence hashes. They persist across restarts.
1894	
1895	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}/runs/{run_id}/audit-records` —
1896	  append a record. Body contains exactly `event`, `input_summary` and
1897	  `result_summary`, each a string that is non-empty after trimming whitespace.
1898	  Returns `201` with the submitted fields plus `id`, `sequence` (continuous
1899	  from `1` within the run), `run_status` (the run's status at write time:
1900	  `running`/`succeeded`/`failed`), `previous_hash` (`null` for the first
1901	  record, otherwise the previous record's `evidence_hash`), `evidence_hash`
1902	  and `created_at`. Missing, extra, non-string or blank fields → `422` and
1903	  nothing is written; unknown dataset/version/task/run → `404`; a run that
1904	  does not belong to the path task (including one in another version) →
1905	  `422`. Concurrent appends never reuse a sequence or break the chain.
1906	- `GET .../runs/{run_id}/audit-records` — list the run's records in ascending
1907	  `sequence` order. Same `404`/`422` path rules.
1908	- `GET .../runs/{run_id}/audit-records/verify` — verify the chain. Returns the
1909	  path identifiers together with `valid` and `checked_count`:
1910	  `{"dataset", "version", "task_id", "run_id", "valid", "checked_count"}`.
1911	  Verification recomputes every `evidence_hash`, checks that `sequence` values
1912	  are continuous from `1` and that each `previous_hash` equals the preceding
1913	  record's `evidence_hash` (the first must be `null`). An intact chain returns
1914	  `"valid": true` (also for an empty chain).
1915	
1916	`evidence_hash` is the hexadecimal SHA-256 of a canonical JSON document built
1917	from every stored field except `id`, `created_at` and `evidence_hash` itself
1918	(`event`, `input_summary`, `result_summary`, `sequence`, `run_status`,
1919	`previous_hash`): keys are sorted by Unicode code point, no insignificant
1920	whitespace is emitted and the text is UTF-8 encoded.
1921	
1922	### Processing run snapshot evidence bindings (append-only proof chain)
1923	
1924	A run can bind the snapshots it consumes and produces as evidence. Each
1925	binding pins one existing, non-deleted snapshot of the run's dataset to the
1926	run as `input` or `output`; bindings form an independent append-only,
1927	tamper-evident hash chain per run (separate from the run's audit-record
1928	chain, which they never read or modify), numbered from `1` per run, linked
1929	through SHA-256 hashes and persisted across restarts. The database rejects
1930	updates and deletes of bindings, and there are no per-binding HTTP routes.
1931	
1932	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/processing-tasks/{task_id}/runs/{run_id}/snapshot-bindings` —
1933	  bind one snapshot. Body contains exactly `role`, `version` and
1934	  `snapshot_id`: `{"role": "input", "version": 1, "snapshot_id": 7}`. `role`
1935	  is exactly `input` or `output` (no trimming); `version` and `snapshot_id`
1936	  are integers (booleans rejected) naming a version of the path dataset and
1937	  a snapshot that currently exists in it. Returns `201` with `id`,
1938	  `sequence` (continuous from `1` within the run), `role`, `dataset`,
1939	  `version`, `snapshot_id`, `run_status` (the run's status at bind time:
1940	  `running`/`succeeded`/`failed`), `previous_hash` (`null` for the first
1941	  binding, otherwise the previous binding's `evidence_hash`),
1942	  `evidence_hash` and `created_at`. A run may carry many bindings; the same
1943	  snapshot may be bound once per role, and a second binding of the same
1944	  `(role, snapshot_id)` to the run returns `409` and writes nothing. The
1945	  bound snapshot may belong to any version of the same dataset (the path
1946	  version only names the task/run). The path dataset/version/task resolves
1947	  first (`404`); a missing, extra or wrongly typed field, an illegal `role`,
1948	  an empty/malformed/non-object body or any query parameter is then a `422`;
1949	  the run must then exist (`404`) and belong to the path task (`422`,
1950	  including a run of a task in another version); only afterwards is the
1951	  body's version/snapshot resolved — a version missing from the dataset, a
1952	  snapshot that does not exist in it or one already confirmed deleted is a
1953	  `404`. Every rejection performs zero writes and never changes the run's
1954	  audit-record chain. Concurrent binds never reuse or skip a sequence.
1955	- `GET .../runs/{run_id}/snapshot-bindings` — list the run's bindings in
1956	  ascending `sequence` order (an empty chain is `[]`). Same `404`/`422`
1957	  path rules; the read takes no body and no query parameters (`422`,
1958	  checked after the path resolves).
1959	- `GET .../runs/{run_id}/snapshot-bindings/verify` — verify the chain,
1960	  returning `{"dataset", "version", "task_id", "run_id", "valid",
1961	  "checked_count", "problems"}`. Verification recomputes every
1962	  `evidence_hash`, checks that `sequence` values are continuous from `1`,
1963	  that the first `previous_hash` is `null` and every later one equals the
1964	  preceding binding's `evidence_hash`, and that each bound snapshot still
1965	  exists. `problems` is sorted by `sequence` then `code`; each item has
1966	  exactly `sequence`, `binding_id` and `code`, and `code` is one of
1967	  `sequence_gap`, `previous_hash_mismatch`, `hash_mismatch` and
1968	  `snapshot_deleted`. Deleting a snapshot after it was bound never changes
1969	  or removes the binding: the chain stays complete and verify reports
1970	  `snapshot_deleted` with `"valid": false`. An empty chain is valid with
1971	  `"checked_count": 0` and no problems. The endpoint takes no body and no
1972	  query parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version/task/run → `404`, a run
1973	  owned by another task → `422`, and an unknown path → `404`.
1974	
1975	A binding's `evidence_hash` is the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of a
1976	canonical JSON document built from `sequence`, `role`, `dataset`,
1977	`version`, `snapshot_id`, `run_status` and `previous_hash` (excluding `id`,
1978	`created_at` and `evidence_hash` itself): keys are sorted by Unicode code
1979	point, no insignificant whitespace is emitted and the text is UTF-8 encoded.
